title: We might be the last programmers who ever lived

beats.text: We might be the last programmers who ever lived.
Look at the code we write today. More and more of it isn't typed by us.
In 2023, GitHub said Copilot was already writing forty-six percent of developers' code where it's switched on.
Ada Lovelace wrote the first program in 1843. FORTRAN let us write code in words in 1957. In 2021, machines started writing it for us. So what comes next?
Partly true. Machines write more of the code every year. But someone still decides what to build, and checks that it's right.

sources: GitHub blog, 14 Feb 2023: 'GitHub Copilot ... behind an average of 46% of a developers' code across all programming languages' (in files where it is enabled)
Ada Lovelace, Note G (1843); FORTRAN released by IBM (1957); GitHub Copilot technical preview (June 2021)
